title: Frontend entry domain http caching cors
topic: Frontend entry domain http caching cors
question: From a frontend developer's point of view, what do HTTP caching headers and CORS each control, and why do they matter when building a web app that talks to an API?
idealAnswer:
Caching headers like Cache-Control (e.g. max-age, no-cache, no-store) tell the browser and intermediate caches how long a response can be reused before it must be re-fetched or revalidated

ETag and Last-Modified support revalidation, letting the browser ask 'has this changed?' and get a cheap 304 Not Modified instead of re-downloading the full response

Poorly set caching can cause stale UI (users seeing old data or old JS bundles after a deploy) or wasted bandwidth (nothing being cached at all)

CORS is a browser-enforced security mechanism controlling whether JavaScript running on one origin can read a response from a different origin, the server opts in via Access-Control-Allow-Origin and related headers

CORS errors happen client-side in the browser console even though the request often actually reached the server, the fix is on the server (or a proxy), not something the frontend can bypass alone

Preflight OPTIONS requests are sent automatically by the browser for 'non-simple' requests (custom headers, certain methods/content-types) to check permissions before the real request is sent
